title: ACEF Incident Report Payload (v1.1 overlay)
description: The v1.1 incident_report payload overlay (RFC-0002 §5.1; Appendix E Revision-3 note: 'the v1.1 incident_report overlay adds ONLY the private card_source block'). This is a FAITHFUL ADDITIVE SUPERSET of the frozen acef-conventions/v1/incident_report.schema.json payload: every v1.0 incident_report field is preserved verbatim, the v1.0 required set ([incident_type, severity, description]) is unchanged, and additionalProperties stays true — so a v1.0-valid incident_report (with NO card_source) validates UNCHANGED under this overlay. The ONLY addition is the optional, now-VALIDATED card_source property, which $refs the v1.1 incident_report.card_source.schema.json closed projection-source block. Before this overlay existed, v1.1 incident_report validation fell back to the frozen v1/ schema (additionalProperties: true), so a payload.card_source of {} was silently accepted and NEVER checked; under the overlay, when card_source is present it is validated against incident_report.card_source.schema.json, so an empty card_source ({}) is REJECTED (its requireds public_incident_id/id_grade/id_state/harm_core/publishability_map/eu_ai_act_facts fail). Gated on manifest.versioning.core_version 1.1.0; the frozen v1/ payload is byte-unchanged. The privileged-analysis fields (root_cause_analysis, lessons_learned, corrective_actions, impact_assessment) remain on incident_report and are NEVER part of card_source's public projection (§5.11). Production resolver/record-type wiring (registry.py, validate_record_payload) is F-M2-SCHEMA-GATING's scope; this file authors the overlay schema only.

occurrence_date.description: Date the incident occurred (ISO 8601), if different from detection.

resolution_date.description: Date the incident was resolved (ISO 8601). Null if unresolved.

root_cause_analysis.description: Root cause analysis of the incident.

responsible_party.description: Person or team responsible for the action.

affected_users_count.description: Number of users affected by the incident.

notification_timeline.description: Order-SIGNIFICANT (RFC-0002 §5.10): the SOLE order-significant array exception — element order is meaningful and MUST NOT be sorted before hashing (unlike every other order-insensitive incident array). Timeline of regulatory and stakeholder notifications (GPAI Art. 55 requires 2-15 day notification).

recipient.description: Who was notified (e.g., 'AI Office', 'national authority', 'affected users').

ai_office_reference.description: AI Office reference number for the incident report.

preventive_measures.description: Preventive measures implemented to avoid recurrence.

impact_assessment.description: Assessment of the impact of the incident on health, safety, or fundamental rights.

regulatory_compliance_impact.description: Assessment of how the incident affects regulatory compliance status.

card_source.description: OPTIONAL v1.1 addition (§5.1): the private projection-source block from which a public incident_card is generated. When present it is validated against the closed incident_report.card_source.schema.json overlay, so an empty card_source ({}) is REJECTED (its six requireds fail). Absent on a v1.0-style report, which validates unchanged. The CONFIDENTIAL/embargoed Art.73 critical path (§5.7) runs entirely source-backed through card_source.eu_ai_act_facts and produces no public card.
